items.title: Hey Poor Player Holiday Buyer’s Guide 2026 – In Case You Missed It
items.summary: 2025 Games Still Exist We’re back yet again with another year of our Holiday Buyer’s Guide. There are no truly bad years for video games. Even with all the turmoil going on in the industry in the last several years, there are still dozens of fantastic games releasing each month,…
items.content:
We're currently experiencing technical difficulties. Please bear with us!

We’re back yet again with another year of our Holiday Buyer’s Guide. There are no truly bad years for video games. Even with all the turmoil going on in the industry in the last several years, there are still dozens of fantastic games releasing each month, and 2026 has been no exception. While one major game may dominate a lot of the discourse this holiday season, we’re here to share what you should look to get your loved ones if they’re looking for more than just that one massive title.

2026 has been an excellent year for video games, but 2025 was too. It’s easy to stay focused on what is new and shiny, but there will always be great games that came out in previous years, and a lot of the time you can grab them a year later for bargain prices. Here are some of the best games of 2025 that would be great to grab for a friend who missed out on them.

What a clever game. Blue Prince is a brilliant twist on roguelikes that has you navigating your way through your family’s ancestral home, solving puzzles and plotting your way around. The deeper you go into the game, the more depth you find as it soon becomes apparent that almost everything here is a puzzle. There are puzzles on top of puzzles on top of puzzles. The game really hits when you notice something you’ve seen at least thirty times before and suddenly realize it matters. Keep a notebook on hand.

Making turn-based RPGs mainstream again was perhaps not on my bingo card for 2025, nor was a game from an unknown developer somehow becoming the juggernaut of last year, but here we are. It did it thanks to a brilliantly realized world, enchanting characters, a stunning soundtrack, and a game that actually has something to say. There are great RPGs every year if you’re not beholden to the AAA style of this one, but if you haven’t played a traditional RPG in a few years, I can’t think of a better way to return to the genre.

Every platform dreams of having a true system seller available at launch. For the Switch 2, that was intended to be the new Mario Kart , and for a lot of players that was enough. Still, the Switch 2’s true system seller came just a month after the system launched and reminded us why Donkey Kong is one of Nintendo’s longest-running characters. The joy of smashing the world around you is something games have played with for decades. I still remember how awesome it was when Red Faction let you damage the environment back on the PS2. Bananza takes that to the extreme, though, as you can smash pretty much the entire world. That there are so many things to find, though, and so much variety to the levels you smash your way through, is what keeps this game compelling and made it our Game of the Year last year.

Platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, Switch, PC

Hades was a big act to follow as one of the most popular roguelike titles ever made. That the team at Supergiant managed to arguably make an even better sequel is one of the most impressive things any game managed to do in 2026. Introducing a new protagonist in Melinoe, the sister of the first game’s Zagreus, who had a new quest and a new reason to make run after run through the fields of the underworld, Hades II again is filled with wonderful characters and a deeply compelling quest. It also expands the first game’s combat and world with new abilities, new boons, and a game that in some ways feels like they gave us Hades II and Hades III in one game. It’s an absolute must-play.

After years of the Silent Hill series sitting fallow, a few years ago it proved it had a place in modern gaming with an excellent remake of Silent Hill 2 . Remaking a game is one thing, though; giving fans a brand new installment is an entirely different one. Silent Hill f has a different feel from most of the series by virtue of moving to 1960s Japan, but the setting ends up being one of the game’s greatest strengths as it tells a tale of love, betrayal, and longing that absolutely shredded us. The atmosphere is phenomenal, and it plays well too, with some fun twists on the Silent Hill formula that make it stand on its own while adding to the legacy of one of gaming’s great horror franchises.

items.title: “I sincerely hope” Rockstar workers succeed: Expedition 33 writer on GTA 6 job fears
items.summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has voiced support for Rockstar workers seeking union recognition, after a developer described
items.content:
This article needs JavaScript to display. Please turn on JavaScript in your browser and reload the page. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has voiced support for Rockstar workers seeking union recognition, after a developer described concerns about job security around the launch of GTA 6.

Her comments focus on a question that can be easy to miss amid a blockbuster release: how much of a successful game’s value reaches the people who made it, and what happens to a team when the most intense stage of development ends?

There is a distinction worth making at the outset. Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte wrote in The Guardian before launch that there was no indication layoffs were coming. He was describing a concern, not announcing job cuts.

GTA 6 launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. Image: Rockstar Games

Svedberg-Yen, who previously worked at Sandfall Interactive, responded to the issue in an Instagram post reported by PC Gamer . She argued that the people creating a game’s value do not necessarily receive a proportionate share of it.

The game is set in the fictional state of Leonida. Image: Rockstar Games

She also said, “I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing.” Her remarks are an argument about the industry and its distribution of rewards, rather than evidence that Rockstar has decided to cut the GTA 6 team.

It is an issue that extends beyond one studio. A game can perform well and still leave its creators wondering how staffing will change as work moves from launch to support or a new project.

Rockstar workers in the UK are voting on union recognition. Image: Rockstar Games

Workers at Rockstar’s UK studios are voting on whether their union should receive formal recognition. The ballot is due to close on November 26, according to PC Gamer’s reporting .

Uriarte described the vote as a way for workers to seek a stronger collective voice on issues including security and working conditions. The outcome is not yet known, and it would be premature to treat the vote as a settlement of those questions.

GTA 6 is available on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. Amazon lists the PS5 code-in-box edition , which does not contain a disc and requires a US or Canadian PlayStation account.

We also covered a movement setting for Jason and Lucia that is easy to overlook.

items.title: Expedition 33 lead writer says Grand Theft Auto 6 layoff concerns show that 'people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value'
items.summary: "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing".
items.content:
Action Grand Theft Auto Expedition 33 lead writer says Grand Theft Auto 6 layoff concerns show that 'people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value' News By Rick Lane Published 21 November 2026 "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing".

But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6 's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off."

It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one.

It's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This issue was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July , claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches.

"99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team."

Watch On Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction."

21% of Rockstar staff have been employed by the company for over 10 years, which explains a lot about GTA 6's record-breaking launch Rockstar will hold union vote right on top of Grand Theft Auto 6 release 'We need to come together': On the eve of GTA 6, 1,600 Rockstar workers are voting on unionization Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector.

"I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created."

items.title: GTA 6 Sparked Controversy Over Its TGA 2026 Nominations, but It Still Won’t Be Able to Surpass One of the Best Games of the Decade
items.summary: Even if GTA 6 dominates The Game Awards 2026, it will fall short of the record set by one of the most-nominated games in the event’s history
items.content:
window.__runDeferredScript({"id":"custom-script-8ccaa8a7","src":"https://t.seedtag.com/t/4204-4423-01.js","strategy":"userInteraction","attributes":{}}); WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

We’re approaching the final stretch of the year, which can only mean one thing: awards season has arrived. All eyes are on The Game Awards 2026 , the video game industry’s most high-profile ceremony. And, as usual, Geoff Keighley’s event has already sparked controversy. This time, the presence of Grand Theft Auto 6 has become a major talking point.

The fact that a game that hasn’t officially launched yet is nominated in multiple categories has led many fans to criticize the organization. Their frustration is understandable, but at least those who oppose Rockstar Games’ title can take comfort in one thing: not even the open-world blockbuster will be able to surpass one of the best games of the decade.

On Tuesday, November 17, Geoff Keighley appeared in a special livestream where, as promised, he revealed the complete list of nominees for TGA 2026. We now know which games will compete for GOTY and other awards.

The biggest announcement was that Grand Theft Auto 6 will be competing for the ceremony’s highest honor. Rockstar’s open-world game will have to face major contenders such as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , 007 First Light , Phantom Blade Zero , Control: Resonant , and Resident Evil Requiem .

GTA 6’s presence was expected, as it’s one of the most ambitious and important games in history. However, the fact that it hasn’t officially launched yet led some fans to criticize The Game Awards 2026 organizers.

Rockstar Games’ title will compete in a total of 8 categories, making it the most-nominated release of the year. But even if it takes home every award, it won’t be able to break an impressive record set by one of last year’s contenders.

We’re talking, of course, about Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the acclaimed turn-based RPG developed by independent studio Sandfall Interactive. The game became a sensation in 2025 and received near-perfect scores from both fans and specialized critics. Naturally, that enthusiasm was reflected at The Game Awards.

The project led by Guillaume Broche received 12 nominations at TGA 2025, the highest number in the event’s history. Ultimately, the fantasy RPG published by Kepler Interactive managed to win an impressive 9 awards, including that year’s GOTY.

This means that even if Grand Theft Auto 6 dominates The Game Awards 2026 and wins every category in which it’s nominated, it won’t be able to beat Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ’s record.

GTA 6 won’t be able to surpass Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s record, even if it wins every award for which it’s nominated.

As mentioned above, Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive’s open-world game has a chance to take home a total of 8 awards across 8 different categories. Unlike what happened last year with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , this time GTA 6 won’t compete twice in the same category.

Naturally, the most important nomination is Game of the Year. Grand Theft Auto 6 will also compete for Best Performance thanks to actress Manni L. Perez, who portrays Lucia Caminos. This nomination confirmed the identity of the actress behind the game’s protagonist.

Here are all the categories in which Grand Theft Auto 6 could win an award at TGA 2026:

items.title: 8 Iconic Video Game Villains Who Were Actually Right the Whole Time
items.summary: "Technically correct" is the best kind of correct
items.content:
By Rebecca Corgan Published Nov 14, 2026, 11:44 AM EST Polygon Lists 'Technically correct' is the best kind of correct

Image: BioWare/Electronic Arts Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Grab your gavel: Court is in session for eight of gaming’s most misunderstood villains. Their charges? One occupied planet, one erased painting, one underwater utopia gone to rot, and a truly staggering body count. But, all that aside, what if these bad guys were actually making a somewhat decent point? Read between the lines of their melodramatic monologues, and perhaps you’ll realize that, say, a centuries-long guilt trip over one catastrophic mistake was in fact understandable rationale for wanting to tear the world down and start over. Or not: You get to decide. Just read each villain’s case file below before reaching a verdict — you might not love where the evidence actually points.

[ Ed. note: This article includes spoilers for the endings of many popular AAA games.]

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive The case for him : The Renoir who fights you wants to keep the fantasy alive. The real one just wants his family to stop grieving inside it.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 splits its central antagonist, Renoir, into two separate people: one painted, one real. The painted-by-Aline Renoir fights alongside Aline to keep the Canvas — and everyone painted into it, including people the expedition has come to love — alive, cutting down anyone who threatens that world. The real Renoir, trapped for years and visibly aged compared to his idealized, painted double, wants the opposite: for the Canvas to end entirely, so the family he’s lost touch with can stop pouring their grief into a fantasy and start healing in reality. Pick a side, and you’re choosing which grieving father’s heartbreak gets to count as the real one.

Image: Irrational Games/2K Games The case for him : His possibly-understandable philosophy never changed. What did was how far he was willing to go once someone else's ambition threatened his city.

Rapture, the underwater city BioShock ’s Andrew Ryan built at the bottom of the Atlantic specifically to escape government oversight and religious interference, was built on one promise: A man’s success belongs to no one but himself. Ryan never walks that back, not even at the very end, when his own death via golf club is on the line. By then, many of his own denizens have curdled into addiction to ADAM, a gene-altering substance Ryan let flourish with zero oversight because, in his mind, oversight was the villain. His by-your-own-bootstraps philosophy never changed, but his willingness to enforce it certainly did — especially once Frank Fontaine’s black market started outcompeting him at his own game.

Image: Obsidian Entertainment The case for her : She spends the game telling you the Jedi and the Sith are both wrong about the same thing. Neither side proves her wrong.

What do you do about a teacher who’s technically right about almost everything…but makes you complicit in her cruelty anyway? Kreia, the blind mentor guiding your player character through Knights of the Old Republic 2 , can see more clearly than the Jedi or Sith about just how broken the galaxy's entire relationship with the Force has become. Her argument is a good one: Total detachment and total hunger are just two different ways of avoiding the same uncomfortable truth about the Force. That said, she also siphons Force energy directly from her companions, weakening them without asking, which is slightly less defensible. And reminiscent of the same casual cost-benefit math that once led her to help gut the Jedi order she claims to be critiquing from a place of wisdom.

Image: Square Enix The case for him : He'll argue his own plan's flaws with you directly, so we have to give him points for more intellectual honesty than we’ve seen from most heroes.

Undo one apocalypse by causing a smaller one! That’s the pitch Emet-Selch spends making in Shadowbringers , the third major expansion for Final Fantasy 14 . He does in fact think this is a good idea. He’ll also spend an evening drinking wine and cracking jokes about the extinction he’s engineering, then recreate the souls of his long-dead friends just to spend one more night with them. Clearly, he’s going through something. Unfortunately, enacting his plan means triggering calamities that gut the present-day population of Eorzea each time, killing real people that you as the player have spent years getting to know, in service of a civilization that’s been dead for thousands of years. To him, this is a solid trade-off — but at what cost to you and those you love?

Image: BioWare/EA via Polygon The case for him : He created the wall that trapped his own people, and he's spent centuries trying to reverse that mistake.

Solas spends Dragon Age: Inquisition posing as a humble elven apostate mage traveling with the Inquisitor (your player character). He’s a trusted companion. He might even be your romantic partner. And, it turns out, he’s actually Fen’Harel, the Dread Wolf of elven legend. The Veil separating the physical world of Thedas from the sometimes-problem-causing spirit realm is something he built himself, thousands of years ago, to end a war between ancient elven gods. To give him a little credit, this worked. But it also cut his people off from their own immortality, dooming the elves to a fall their descendants can’t even remember. Solas does cry and apologize as he’s revealing what he’s done, but does feeling bad about doing something horrifying wipe his slate clean? (I haven’t played Dragon Age: The Veilguard yet, but I have heard whispers about Solas’ role in it that suggest I’m onto something here.)

Image: Valve The case for him : He surrendered humanity to an occupation. He also might be the only reason humanity still exists to resent him for it.

items.title: Mass Effect Could Still Be Saved, Ex-BioWare Developer Suggests, With Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Holding the Key
items.summary: The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.
items.content:
The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.

In the days since EA announced it was shutting down its storied RPG game studio and killing its in-development Mass Effect Universe project, discussion has turned to the costs behind creating another AAA-budget entry in BioWare's space opera series, following a report that EA decided to invest in Star Wars instead .

Last week, BioWare co-founder Trent Oster suggested that EA would likely have been on the hook for at least $200 million in development costs to finish Mass Effect Universe at a level that fans expected.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200m+," Oster wrote on X/Twitter. "That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work." (To be fair, there is still that Mass Effect TV series in the works. And there certainly won't be any bigger plan in place for the IP if its flagship next game is cancelled.)

Now, Mass Effect lead programmer Christina Norman has said the game could be made for around $50 million — a figure that is five times the budget spent by the makers of Clair Obscur.

Highlighting a report on the French-made RPG's overall budget, which was pegged at less than $10 million, Norman wrote on X/Twitter that this was "a good example of why I think another Mass Effect game could be made for well under 200 million.

"I mean 5x the budget of Claire obscure expedition 33 should be more than enough," she continued. "You can always spend more but clever small teams can get it done."

Norman spent more than six years at BioWare working on the original Mass Effect trilogy, firstly as a lead programmer responsible for creating the franchise's conversation system, before moving on to become lead designer for Mass Effect 2 and 3, working to improve the series' gameplay.

In the years since, Norman served stints at Riot Games and her own co-founded startup, before becoming a full-time machine learning engineering consultant focused on LLM-directed character conversations. Still, there's no suggestion that LLM technology would be needed to turn in Mass Effect Universe on a smaller budget.

Even Oster has said he believed a new Mass Effect could be made for "cheaper" than $200m, though it "wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept," he wrote in a follow-up post. Alas, Oster also highlighted another big blocker to a new Mass Effect being made — that EA still owns the franchise's rights, and may never want to give them up, even if it's not actively using them. "The big push would be getting the IP free," he concluded. "The fans deserve more."

Last week's annual N7 Day celebration of the Mass Effect franchise featured the Normandy's cast and crew teaming up for a video message asking fans to help save Mass Effect . This followed an array of footage and details for the canceled Mass Effect Universe appearing online, and a petition for EA to reconsider its decision which has gained more than 325,000 signatures . A Canadian politician also started a government petition to save BioWare just last week.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.summary: Introducing a special bundle featuring the award‑winning fantasy RPG “Metaphor: ReFantazio”, created by the team behind Persona 3-5, paired with “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33” - now available at 10% off! Enjoy both titles and experience the
items.content:
Introducing a special bundle featuring the award‑winning fantasy RPG “Metaphor: ReFantazio”, created by the team behind Persona 3-5, paired with “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33” - now available at 10% off!

Enjoy both titles and experience the worlds for yourself!

The Metaphor: ReFantazio × Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Bundle includes two games: “Metaphor: ReFantazio” and “Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.”

Message from Guillaume Broche & Katsura Hashino

"Metaphor: ReFantazio is a game that is really inspiring for us. It tells a beautiful story in a completely new world that is masterfully crafted. It deals with heavy themes but one that resonates strongly with me is the importance of imagination in all aspects of our lives. The cast is lovable and the turn-based battle system is one of the best I have played. The re-imagination of the traditional jobs system through Archetypes is fantastic and opens up so many playstyles that are fun to play around with. On top of that, the game has one of the most charismatic villains I've ever seen in an RPG. It is a great honor to be able to collaborate with Atlus on this bundle, as I have been a fan of their work since Shin Megami Tensei: Lucifer's Call (also known as Shin Megami Tensei III Nocturne for some players)." - Guillaume Broche

"I am Katsura Hashino from ATLUS, serving as the Creative Director for “Metaphor: ReFantazio.” I am very pleased to hear that a Steam bundle will be released with “Expedition 33,” a title that has received high praise around the world.

“Expedition 33” is a work that conveys a deep understanding of and sincere dedication to the JRPG genre, crafted with great care down to the finest details. As someone who also creates RPGs, I found it to be truly inspiring.

I am genuinely delighted to see Japanese-style RPGs being born and embraced, not only from Japanese-based studios like ours, but other places around the world through diverse creative approaches.

While the two titles differ in their worlds and overall direction, players may find a shared spirit in how we each approach and express the RPG genre. I hope that this bundle encourages players to experience both titles and enjoy the breadth of what RPGs can offer."
